---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send messages (text, Block Kit, threads, webhooks), list/create/join/archive channels, look up users, search message history, and upload files. Use when the user asks to post or schedule Slack messages, manage Slack channels, find Slack users, search Slack conversations, automate Slack workflows, or build Slack integrations with a bot token or incoming webhook.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Use the Slack Web API over HTTPS with a bot token (`xoxb-...`) or an incoming webhook URL. Prefer the bundled scripts for deterministic operations (posting, listing channels); call the API directly for ad-hoc queries. Every Web API response is JSON with an `ok` boolean.

## Authentication

- Set the `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable to a bot token (`xoxb-...`). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- If only an incoming webhook URL (`https://hooks.slack.com/services/...`) is available, you can post messages with a simple POST, but no other API methods are available.
- Each method requires scopes on the token (e.g., `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `channels:manage`, `users:read`, `search:read`, `files:write`). An `missing_scope` error names the scope to add in the Slack app settings.

## Quick Start

Post a message using the bundled script:

```bash
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/post_message.cjs --channel "#general" --text "Hello from Gemini CLI"
```

Or directly with curl:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"#general","text":"Hello"}'
```

## Core Operations

### Post Messages

- Use `chat.postMessage` with `channel` (channel name like `#general` or channel/user ID), `text`, optional `blocks` (Block Kit JSON), and `thread_ts` to reply inside a thread.
- Use `chat.postEphemeral` to show a message only to one user, and `chat.update` to edit, `chat.delete` to remove.
- Use `scripts/post_message.cjs` to avoid JSON escaping mistakes; it also supports webhook URLs and `--thread-ts`.

### Manage Channels and Conversations

- `conversations.list` lists channels (paginated). Use `scripts/list_channels.cjs` for a compact, LLM-friendly output.
- `conversations.create` creates a channel; `conversations.join` joins it; `conversations.rename` renames; `conversations.archive` / `conversations.unarchive` toggle archiving.
- `conversations.history` fetches recent messages in a known channel (use `latest`, `oldest`, `limit`).
- Private channels require `types=private_channel`; direct messages require `types=im`; multi-person DMs `types=mpim`.

### Look Up Users

- `users.list` returns workspace members; `users.info` fetches one user by ID; `users.lookupByEmail` converts an email to a user ID.
- To mention a user in a message, use their user ID in the form `<@U123ABC>`.

### Search History

- `search.messages` with queries like `from:@alice after:2024-01-01` or `keyword in:#general`.
- Search can lag behind recent activity; for recent messages in a known channel prefer `conversations.history`.

### Upload Files

- `files.upload` posts a multipart/form-data request with `channels`, `file`, `filename`, and optional `initial_comment`.

## Response Handling

- Check `ok` first. When `false`, `error` holds a short code (see `references/api.md` for common codes).
- On HTTP 429 (`rate_limited`), read the `Retry-After` header and wait that many seconds before retrying.
- List methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; loop with `cursor` until it is empty. The bundled scripts already do this.

## Rate Limits

- Default tier allows roughly 1 request/second per method (some methods 50+/second). For bulk operations, add small delays and keep `limit` parameters modest.

## References

- Read `references/api.md` for the full method reference, Block Kit cheat sheet, message formatting rules, and error codes. Load it when you need details beyond the operations above.
- Read `scripts/post_message.cjs` or `scripts/list_channels.cjs` before modifying them for environment-specific adjustments.

# Slack Web API Reference

Base URL for all methods: `https://slack.com/api/<method>` (POST with JSON body, or GET with query params for read-only methods). Send the bot token as `Authorization: Bearer xoxb-...`.

## Contents

1. [Common Method Reference](#common-method-reference)
2. [Pagination](#pagination)
3. [Rate Limits](#rate-limits)
4. [Error Codes](#error-codes)
5. [Message Formatting](#message-formatting)
6. [Block Kit Cheat Sheet](#block-kit-cheat-sheet)
7. [Incoming Webhooks](#incoming-webhooks)

## Common Method Reference

### chat.postMessage

Post a message to a channel, DM, or thread.

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"#general","text":"Hello","blocks":[{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"Hello *world*"}}]}'
```

Key params: `channel` (name or ID), `text`, `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn` (bool), `unfurl_links`, `icon_emoji`, `username` (override display name).
Scopes: `chat:write`, `chat:write:bot`. Returns `ts` (message timestamp, used as `thread_ts` for replies).

### chat.postEphemeral

Message visible only to one user in a channel. Add `user` param. Scope: `chat:write`.

### chat.update / chat.delete

Edit or remove a message. Requires `channel` + `ts`. Scope: `chat:write`.

### conversations.list

List all channels (paginated). Query params: `types` (`public_channel`, `private_channel`, `im`, `mpim`), `exclude_archived`, `limit` (max 200), `cursor`, `team_id`.
Scopes: `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`.

### conversations.history

Fetch recent messages: `conversations.history?channel=C123&limit=100&oldest=<unix_ts>&latest=<unix_ts>`. Scope: `channels:history`.

### conversations.create / join / leave / rename / archive / unarchive

Channel management. `conversations.create` takes `name` (no `#`). Scopes: `channels:manage`, `groups:write`, `channels:join`.

### users.list / users.info / users.lookupByEmail

- `users.list` — all workspace members (paginated). Scope: `users:read`.
- `users.info?user=U123` — profile for one user.
- `users.lookupByEmail?email=a@b.com` — find user ID by email. Scope: `users:read.email`.

### search.messages

`search.messages?query=from:@alice after:2024-01-01 in:#general`. Scope: `search:read`. Note: index may lag; prefer `conversations.history` for recent messages in a known channel.

### files.upload

Multipart/form-data POST with fields `channels` (comma-separated), `file` (binary), `filename`, `initial_comment`, `title`. Scope: `files:write`.

### reactions.add / pins.add

Add emoji reaction (`reactions.add` with `channel`, `name`, `timestamp`) or pin a message (`pins.add`). Scopes: `reactions:write`, `pins:write`.

## Pagination

List methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Loop until it is empty:

```bash
curl -s "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?limit=200&cursor=$CURSOR" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"
```

The bundled `list_channels.cjs` script handles this automatically.

## Rate Limits

- Default tier: ~1 request/second per method; some methods allow 50+/second.
- Bulk operations: add small delays and keep `limit` small.
- On HTTP 429, honor the `Retry-After` header (seconds) before retrying.

## Error Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token is invalid or revoked |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a required scope (name is in `response_metadata.messages`) |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot must join the channel first (`conversations.join`) |
| `channel_not_found` | Channel name/ID does not exist |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive first |
| `rate_limited` | Too many requests; honor `Retry-After` |
| `too_many_attachments` | Message payload too large; trim `blocks` |
| `invalid_blocks` | Block Kit JSON is malformed |

## Message Formatting

- **Mention user**: `<@U123ABC>`
- **Link channel**: `<#C123|general>`
- **Bold**: `*text*`; **italic**: `_text_`; **code**: `` `text` ``
- **Inline link**: `<https://example.com|Click here>`
- **Emoji**: `:tada:`, `:+1:`
- Newlines in `text` render as line breaks when `mrkdwn` is enabled (default).

## Block Kit Cheat Sheet

Blocks are the structured message format; `text` becomes a fallback. Common blocks:

```json
{
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "section", "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Hello <@U123ABC>" } },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Choose an option:" },
      "accessory": {
        "type": "button",
        "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Click" },
        "action_id": "button_1",
        "value": "clicked"
      }
    },
    { "type": "image", "image_url": "https://example.com/img.png", "alt_text": "image" },
    { "type": "context", "elements": [{ "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Posted by a bot" }] }
  ]
}
```

## Incoming Webhooks

Given a webhook URL, post messages without a token:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text":"Hello","blocks":[...]}'
```

Webhooks accept `text` and `blocks` only; other API methods are not available.
